messages:
Marta: Heads-up from nightly eval — the billing-clarify prompt set regressed against redwood-v2-quant (q4) overnight. Was ~1 fail, now 12. Generations look split/misaligned across runs (same prompt, different answers).

ci-bot: nightly-eval job #8472 completed at 2026-03-19T03:12Z. Summary: 12 failing prompts (prev 1). Report: https://ci/reports/nightly/8472 — artifacts attached.

Devin: can you paste one failing example output + the run metadata (model, quant, batch config, routing)?

Marta: sure — example below (two runs, same prompt):

```
Prompt: "Can you summarize the latest billing changes for API usage?"
Run A: "The new billing increases the token price by 20%. For invoices, see the billing portal..."
Run B: "We applied a pro-rated adjustment. Note: billing portal updated 03/15. Follow steps: 1) go to settings..."
```

Meta: model=redwood-v2-quant-q4, quantize_profile=q4_8bit, routing=hosted-prod, batching_policy=async_continuous, cache=prefix_kv (trunc=64), seed=auto

Raj: I dug into the artifacts. Reproduced locally with the same model+quant. When I run with `--batch-size=1 --batching-policy=sync_accumulate` outputs are stable, but with `--batch-size=64 --batching-policy=async_continuous` the outputs diverge across retries.

Raj: hypothesis: KV prefix cache key truncation + cache eviction order (due to batching interleaving) is returning the wrong prefix KV occasionally — effectively serving a prefix from a different tenant/request order, which changes context and sampling.

Devin: hmm. Do we have the exact cache key function?

Marta: current key: `key = sha256(prefix_bytes || model_id || trunc(tenant_id,64bits))` (we truncate for smaller index size). We also use LRU eviction per-shard. Batching changes the order keys are looked up and maybe evicted/inserted in between asynchronous loads.

Eva: two quick ideas: 1) stop truncating tenant_id (or increase truncation bits), 2) namespace by tenant (prepend tenant salt to key) so collisions are impossible even if truncation stays. Also ensure we never reuse a cached KV without verifying `prefix_length` and `model_version` fields.

Samir: ran a tiny ablation: added tenant salt prefix plus a compact hash (still 64b) and ran 200 samples from the failing prompt set with batching=64 async. Failures dropped 12->0 in that sample. Diff: https://replay/sam/kvfix-123

Raj: nice. Also found an unrelated issue: RNG state is currently global per-worker and we *don't* reset sampling RNG after a cache-hit path vs cold path, so interleaving can leak sampling state between requests when using shared workers. I pushed a small patch to snapshot/restore Philox per-request.

Marta: good catch. So two-pronged: tighten namespace for cache keys and isolate per-request RNG. Which should we roll to nightly first? Any perf impact?

Samir: tenant-salt change is config-only and has negligible perf impact (cache hit rate drops ~0.6% in our microbench). The RNG snapshot has tiny CPU cost on request start (~0.2ms). I opened PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/539 (tenant-salt) and https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/540 (rng-snapshot).

Devin: let's hotfix nightly: merge tenant-salt first (safer), enable on the nightly cluster, then rerun full nightly. If green, plan a canary to prod-dedicated and measure hit-rate.

Marta: agreed. I'll merge PR 539 after a quick review and schedule a rerun of nightly-eval. Also adding an assertion in eval harness to detect cross-tenant KV reuse: `assert(kv.prefix_tenant == request.tenant)` so we catch regressions.

ci-bot: rerun scheduled: nightly-eval #8472-rerun at 2026-03-19T03:36Z.

Eva: note for follow-up: we should also audit any truncation logic in the indexer — make truncation config per-index and track collision metrics.

Samir: quick stats from local smoke: before fix: 12/50 fails; after tenant-salt: 0/50; after rng-snapshot: still 0/50. Will run bigger run tonight.

Marta: thanks all. Keeping thread open — if the rerun shows any residuals we'll triage eviction concurrency and consider switching to deterministic synchronous batch ordering for hot paths. :eyes:
